# OpenSound

> Unofficial, GPL-3.0-or-later Linux controller for WH-1000XM5 headphones. A Rust daemon speaks the MDR v2 protocol over Bluetooth RFCOMM and exposes a session D-Bus API, used by a GTK 4 / libadwaita app and a GNOME Shell extension. Non-profit; built because no official Linux option exists. Not affiliated with Sony.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): features, install, D-Bus API, legal notice
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): architecture, commands, code style, protocol and safety rules for AI agents
- [Protocol reference](docs/PROTOCOL.md): framing, commands, confirmation alerts
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): workflow, device reports, AI-assisted contributions
- [Disclaimer](DISCLAIMER.md): no affiliation, trademarks, no warranty

## Source

- [crates/opensound-core/src/frame.rs](crates/opensound-core/src/frame.rs): frame codec
- [crates/opensound-core/src/protocol.rs](crates/opensound-core/src/protocol.rs): pure request builders, reply parser and state model
- [crates/opensound-daemon/src/link.rs](crates/opensound-daemon/src/link.rs): RFCOMM link with ACK handling
- [crates/opensound-daemon/src/main.rs](crates/opensound-daemon/src/main.rs): D-Bus service
- [crates/opensound-gtk/src/main.rs](crates/opensound-gtk/src/main.rs): GTK app
- [packaging/opensound.spec](packaging/opensound.spec): Fedora package
- [gnome-extension/opensound@cpujp.github.io/extension.js](gnome-extension/opensound@cpujp.github.io/extension.js): GNOME Shell extension
